coordinateSystem: +Z is the rotation pole placed in the plane of the sky at the ALMA position angle; +X is the display meridian, set so that grid longitude 0 faces the Sun and Earth at the scene epoch; east longitude.
source: Kervella et al. (2018, A&A 609, A67; arXiv:1711.07983): ALMA CO and SiO line emission give the north pole a position angle PA = 48.0 +/- 3.5 deg east of north and a rotation period P/sin i = 36 +/- 8 years. The inclination i is not measured there, so the pole is placed perpendicular to the line of sight (sin i = 1) from the SIMBAD J2000 position; 36 years is 315576 hours. Uitenbroek, Dupree & Gilliland (1998, AJ 116, 2501) instead argued from a Hubble bright spot that the pole points about 20 deg from the line of sight; that alternative is recorded, not adopted. The display meridian W is the sub-solar east longitude the IAU node convention would otherwise give (-9.923 degrees), so the hemisphere the photograph covers is the one shown lit; there is no measured prime meridian.
